clue.text: The classroom is prepared by him?

definitions.text: The classroom is prepared by him?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether the person who readies the classroom each morning is the man in charge of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is prepared' rearranges THE CLASSROOM; read whole, the clue also describes the answer, as he gets the classroom ready for lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a male teacher, the person who readies a classroom for pupils.

clue.text: Kid pinches exceptionally good apple

indicators.note: pinches means grips between, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to kid is to cod, both meaning to hoax or tease
a star performer is exceptionally good

explanation.surface: A child steals a particularly fine apple from a fruit stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to fool, which is COD in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A costard is a large old English variety of cooking apple.

clue.text: Check the wickets taken in a batch of deliveries

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler
a bowler's haul is the number of wickets he takes

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer checks how many wickets fell during one over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six balls bowled in turn, and a bowler's HAUL is his tally of wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to examine it thoroughly and repair it, a full check.

clue.text: Top instrument, old instrument

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a flute is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: Contrasts a leading modern instrument with an antique one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective meaning best, but is a verb: behead FLUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked stringed instrument popular in Renaissance Europe, now largely historical.

clue.text: Tar producing a mark not making one cross?

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
staining is leaving a mark or blot

explanation.surface: A sailor who leaves a smear is not a cross sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross is the X on a ballot paper: a voter who abstains makes no cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone declining to vote puts no X mark on the ballot paper.

clue.text: Toned down thanks to the sea

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Something became calmer because of the soothing sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamed and toned down both mean made milder or less wild.

clue.text: Trusty heart of weld in restored train

indicators.note: in places the middle letters inside the rearranged word
restored means put back together in a new order, so the letters of train are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A dependable welding job at the centre of repairing a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes EL from weld; 'restored' rearranges TRAIN into RIANT; 'in' puts EL inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant means dependent on or trusting in, and so trusty in the sense of placing trust.

clue.text: A writer? He'll be one carol, possibly

annotationWithheld.why: A writer? He'll be one carol, possibly (7,6): fodder HE'LL BE + one (I) + CAROL is one I short of HILAIREBELLOC; no source found for the true wording
annotationWithheld.clue: A writer? He'll be one carol, possibly

clue.text: Very depressed: could be earthed

parts.note: read as wordplay: the word hearted, broken up, could become the clue word earthed

explanation.surface: A gloomy electrician notes that a cable might be earthed.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse clue: HEARTED rearranged gives EARTHED, so HEARTED BROKEN describes the clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person crushed by grief or disappointment is utterly miserable.

clue.text: Examine fashionable glasses? Not half

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: not half means drop half the word, its last five of ten letters

parts.note: spectacles are glasses

explanation.surface: Someone asks to look at trendy eyewear, and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it cuts SPECTACLES in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look over carefully, to scrutinise.

clue.text: A member left in reserve making comeback? Must be embroidery

indicators.note: in puts the group of letters inside the turned word
making a comeback means coming back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A footballer on the bench returns to the team, but it seems he must be needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns RES into SER, which holds A, MP and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is a piece of needlework showing a variety of stitches.

clue.text: Embarrass a party

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: A party leaves someone red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: Book uncompromising footballer

parts.note: a hard line is an uncompromising one
a back is a defending football player

explanation.surface: Reserves a tough defender for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb, to sign up a player, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers.

clue.text: Senior churchman in leaderless demo with a company in retreat

indicators.note: leaderless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a demo or demonstration is a protest march

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the hideaway word

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A clergyman joins a protest with a firm that is withdrawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' turns MARCH into ARCH; 'in' puts A and CO inside DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a cleric ranking just below a bishop in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Terribly crude r-tirade: could be turned into jelly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of crude are mixed up

parts.note: a stammered tirade, the letter R followed by a rant

explanation.surface: A stuttering rude outburst could be turned into a wobbly dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges CRUDE into REDCU; the stammer puts R before RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The small red fruit is often boiled with sugar to make a preserve set as a jelly.

clue.text: Big star grabs time to produce a knock-out

indicators.note: grabs means seizes and holds, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: the sun is a big star

explanation.surface: A celebrity seizes the moment to deliver a dazzling performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big star' suggests a celebrity, but it is our SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock someone senseless, as a knockout blow does.

clue.text: Put in can and posted to the county

parts.note: a posted letter has been sent
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Something packed in a tin and mailed out to the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for prison; SENT DOWN is British for jailed. DOWN is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jailed is to be locked up, and can is slang for prison.

clue.text: Made draught a certain colour, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said out loud, standing for one spelt differently

parts.note: blue is a colour

explanation.surface: A painter turns a draught board a particular shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow is to create a current of air, so blew is produced a draught.

clue.text: Takes into service books

definitions.meaning: reserves, as a performer or a table

explanation.surface: An employer hires staff and orders reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging staff is hiring them; engaging a band is booking it in advance.

clue.text: Each bangle is refined in fluid

indicators.note: refined means reworked or polished, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Each bracelet is purified by dipping in liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid in the sense of shifting and unsettled, never fixed.

clue.text: Bird seen in the marshes when it's freezing to the north

parts.note: bitter weather is freezing cold

explanation.surface: A wading bird appears in the wetlands in harsh northern winters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' sits N below BITTER in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A bittern is a heron-like wading bird of reed beds, known for its booming call.

clue.text: They receive something for example in city river

indicators.note: in puts the example abbreviation within the city abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: People get things, for instance in a riverside city.
explanation.walkthrough: The TEES is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Legatees are people who are left bequests in a will.

clue.text: Not called up in charge? That's a fillip

indicators.note: up in a down light means read from the bottom, so the word is turned backwards

explanation.surface: A serviceman passed over for call-up still feels a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called up' suggests military call-up, but it reverses NOT to TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is anything that invigorates or gives a lift.

clue.text: Teach part of bible in routine on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the whole is read backwards
in puts the testament abbreviation inside the word for routine

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Instruct a scripture class during the routine trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OT inside RUT, making ROTUT; 'on the way back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to instruct privately.

clue.text: Some signed item to prepare for publication

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an autographed article is readied for print.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise and correct a text before it is published.

clue.text: Chemical-free living?

definitions.meaning: grown without artificial fertilisers or pesticides

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lifestyle free of chemicals counts as natural living.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is farmed without synthetic chemicals; organic matter comes from living things.

clue.text: Ice does melt, see!

indicators.note: melt means lose shape, so the letters of the first two words run into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation at ice thawing before your eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see!' looks like an exclamation but is the noun: a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area under a bishop's authority.

clue.text: Support the negative in colour. It's the best

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it

indicators.note: in places the negative word inside the colour word

parts.note: a tone is a shade of colour
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Backing a negative image in colour produces the finest result.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbeaten by anything else, the top of its kind.
